title: compliance-carryon-scratch-lin-2026
content:
Quick brain-dump: SOC2 prep orientation + checklist fragments (personal scratchpad). Use this to prep tabletop + to collect minimal evidence set for Dedicated and Private customers. Not polished — notes to self.

Context / intention:
- We need a minimal, repeatable evidence kit for the most common auditor requests (access logs, key rotation receipts, change approvals, incident timeline). Focus first on controls we know auditors zero in on: logical access, change mgmt, encryption/keys, monitoring/alerts, backups/restoration, and vendor mgmt.
- Keep separate flows for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (customer-managed KMS edges).

Open questions to resolve quickly:
- For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers where key material never leaves customer KMS, what evidence do we provide? snapshot of config + signed attestation from infra customer onboarding engineer? need legal signoff.
- Can we provide time-bounded access logs for model inference requests without leaking customer data? approach: tokenized request ids + request metadata (latency, model version, route) in logs; redact PII. Confirm with privacy team.
- Where are final Signed Runbooks stored? current: a mix of Confluence + /secure-s3/attestations (ugh). Need single source-of-truth.

Immediate mapping idea (very rough):
- CC6 / Logical access: AAD/Okta user provisioning, MFA enforced, SSO SAML configs, role bindings in Console (admin, observer, operator). Evidence: Okta export, recent user provisioning ticket (JIRA: ID), sample policy JSON from Console, screenshot + audit event for 'revoke' action.
- CC7 / Change management: PR + CI/CD pipeline traces for infra changes. Evidence: GitHub PR, Jenkins/CI job logs, rollout record from Console (rollout ID + timestamp), approval comments. Need to standardize: required labels ("security-approved") before merge — add to PR template.
- CC5 / System operations & availability: autoscaling config snapshot, SLA dashboard screenshot, paging history (PagerDuty runbook ID). Evidence: dashboard with last 90 days, incident postmortem.
- CC3 / Confidentiality & encryption: key rotation logs, KMS policy snapshot, data-in-rest encryption config for model artifacts + cache. Evidence: rotation event in KMS audit logs + policy JSON.
- CC4 / Monitoring & detection: central logs (ELK/Datadog), alert defs, retention policy, sample alert + response ticket. Evidence: alert rule export + linked PD incident.

Evidence collection templates (ideas):
- Access control evidence bundle: CSV export (user, role, created_at, last_auth) + screen capture of active sessions + JIRA ticket for user deprovisioning request.
- Change mgmt bundle: PR link, CI run id, diff snapshot, reviewer list, deployment rollout id, canary metrics snapshot.
- KMS bundle: key-id, policy digest, rotation timestamps (ISO8601), who initiated rotation (svc account or human), signed attestation for customer-managed keys.
- Backups: backup manifest (timestamped), restore test log (who performed, time to restore, success/failure), retention policy doc.

Notes on Private deployments (edge cases):
- Customer provides their KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure/HSM). We must show we never store plaintext material and that our software reads keys at runtime. Evidence: code snippet (config loading), diagram of key flow, acceptance checklist signed by infra eng.
- When customer requests export of audit logs, prep anonymization script that strips any customer content but retains metadata required by auditor. Track request in ticket (CS-XXXXX).

Tabletop ideas for next session (30–45m):
- Scenario A: revoked admin key discovered — steps to revoke, rotate, re-encrypt, notify customer, update runbook. Who does what? aim to produce an incident timeline + artifacts in 2 hours.
- Scenario B: failed automatic rotation (job timed out) — can we rollback? evidence: job logs + mitigation steps.
- Scenario C: model-serving node leaked disk snapshot — we must show encryption at rest + proof of no cleartext logs. Run a dry-run: replicate steps to verify.

To-dos (very tangible):
- [ ] centralize runbooks into /secure-confluence/trust-ops/runbooks (owner: Ramon) — due 2026-03-19
- [ ] create PR template additions to require security label + link to JIRA attestation ticket (owner: DevInfra team) — open GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/501
- [ ] generate 3 sample evidence bundles for Hosted, Dedicated, Private (owner: me — Lin) — due 2026-03-26
- [ ] privacy review for log redaction approach (owner: Aisha) — pinged via slack #privacy on 2026-03-05

Short snippets / scripts we might need (notes-to-self):
- Redaction: script takes raw log lines -> replaces any string matching email regex /\b[\w.%+-]+@[\w.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,6}\b/ with <REDACTED_EMAIL>, drop request-body if contains model_input key.
- Evidence packager: tar + sha256sum + signed metadata.json (fields: id, created_by, components[]). Need signing key from trust-ops KMS (service account).

Potential auditor questions (prep answers):
- Q: "How do you ensure only authorized employees can access customer keys?" A: outline SSO + RBAC + ephemeral access tokens + SRE-approved bastion for emergency access; note that Private customers keep keys — explain attestation and onboarding checklist.
- Q: "Show me proof of a recent key rotation and verification." A: provide KMS rotation event, rotation verification script output, and deployment rollout id.
- Q: "How do you detect anomalous model outputs or exfil attempts?" A: monitoring on request sizes, unusual throughput spikes, anomaly detection on embedding similarity distributions.

Random heuristics / thoughts:
- Keep evidence minimal but sufficient: auditors want to see process + artifacts that prove process actually executed. Not every log line.
- When in doubt, timestamp everything and link to immutable IDs (S3 object, PR number, PD incident id).
- Favor snapshots + signed metadata.

Possible artifacts to produce this week (practical list):
1) Example access-export.csv (include header + 5 redacted rows)
2) KMS rotation event export for test key + rotation verification runbook (markdown)
3) Change mgmt PR bundle (PR diff + CI logs + Console rollout screenshot)
4) Backup + restore test log for small test cluster (timestamped)

Slack refs / tickets mentioned during notes:
- slack: #trust-ops thread: "soc2-evidence-req" (see pinned messages)
- jira: INF-2382 (evidence automation), CS-882 (customer request for log export), PD-1173 (recent pager for uptime hit)

End-of-day micro-scope: produce 1 minimal evidence bundle for Hosted (access control + one rotation event) and write short README explaining how to reproduce packaging. If I can finish that, it's easier to adapt for Dedicated/Private.

——
Notes to self (final): keep this messy. When I convert to a 'real' document, split into: evidence matrix, runbooks (indexed), automation scripts, and demo checklist. For now, keep brainstorming here and annotate during tabletop.

Lin
2026-03-12
